sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups for 'my requests' per employee; status: filtering pending/approved/rejected queues; manager approval inbox; leave_type_id: filtering by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); start_date, end_date: date-range scans for calendar views and overlap/conflict detection; approved_by: manager's approval queue lookups; (employee_id, status): compound filter for employee-specific status queries; (status, start_date): sorted approval queues by date

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: balance lookups per employee (most frequent access pattern); policy_id: policy-driven balance queries; fiscal_year: scoping balances to a fiscal year; (employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year): unique-lookup compound — one balance row per employee per policy per year; also used for accrual/consumption updates; (employee_id, fiscal_year): employee's annual balance summary across all leave types

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup for auth and notifications; manager_id: team listing — find all direct reports of a manager; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees; department: department-scoped queries

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering active policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filtering only active policies for entitlement lookups; (leave_type, is_active): common compound filter for policy resolution

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookup for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT); (entity_type, entity_id, performed_at): chronological audit trail for an entity

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: fetching notifications for a specific user; status: filtering unread/pending notifications; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: finding notifications tied to a specific leave request or entity; (recipient_id, status): inbox queries — unread notifications for a user

data_notes: Persistence slice defined with 6 conceptual tables (leave_requests, leave_balances, employees, leave_policies, audit_logs, notifications) and 6 repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by the existing pg Pool. Two open questions recorded: day-counting semantics (calendar vs business days) and fiscal-year boundary — both materially affect balance arithmetic and must be resolved before the code agent writes queries.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — calendar days or business/working days?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction (used_days increment), overlap/conflict detection, entitlement display, and the duration calculation in every query that sums or compares leave spans. If calendar days, a Friday–Monday leave consumes 4 days; if business days, it consumes 2.
candidate_options: Business days (Mon–Fri only, excluding public holidays)
Business days excluding public holidays (requires holiday calendar)

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal-year boundary for leave balances?
open_questions.impact: Determines which balance row is used for a given leave request. If the fiscal year is calendar (Jan 1–Dec 31), a December 28–January 3 leave spans two balance rows. If it follows a different cycle (e.g. Apr 1–Mar 31), the same date range may fall within a single row. Affects balance lookup, accrual scheduling, and carry-over logic.
